summary: This tutorial introduces Mozilla Thunderbird, a simple email client available on multiple platforms. It covers downloading and launching Thunderbird, configuring new email accounts, reading and writing emails, and sending messages. Thunderbird supports various email folders and address books, and can consolidate POP3 accounts from different providers like Gmail and Yahoo into a single inbox using specific features. The tutorial demonstrates setting up Thunderbird on Ubuntu Linux 12.04. To use Thunderbird, you need at least two valid email accounts with POP3 enabled. Launch Thunderbird by clicking the Thunderbird icon on the desktop. Configure your email accounts through the Mail Account Setup dialog box. For Gmail, log in to your account, open the browser, type www.gmail.com, enter your username and password, then click the settings icon, select settings, and enable POP for all emails. This allows Thunderbird to download your emails from the Gmail account.
